note: Language-neutral statements of the R4H-A transport trust boundary. Each scenario names the exact compiled test that proves it; tests/acceptance_corpus.rs refuses a scenario whose owner is not a real #[test] in the named target. This corpus is A's alone: R4H-L owns fixtures/rust-reconstruction/r4-host-auth-foundation under contract grapt-location-acceptance-corpus/v1, whose validator admits exactly four scenarios in order, so adding a row there would turn that lane red. R4HA-08 rules the separation.

scenarios.claim: A fixture-verified subject resolves server-side to exactly one recipient and one client identity, and the minted principal reports both plus the directory generation it was minted under.
A DTO naming recipient B under seat A's authentication never reads, snapshots, subscribes or emits B; the server-derived recipient is authoritative.
On a route carrying a recipient field, a value disagreeing with the derived recipient is refused before any application call, and a value that agrees grants nothing.
A syntactically valid caller-authored AuthenticatedClientId is refused because of its provenance, not its shape, even when it equals an identity the directory really issued.
With no verified subject the application service is not invoked at all.
A valid, current principal receives a typed authorization refusal for an action no capability proof covers, and the application is not invoked.
After the directory advances a generation, a principal minted under the old generation authorizes nothing, and is refused as stale rather than as unproven.
Configuration beyond max_principal_mappings is refused whole, with no partial directory, and the refusal names the bound rather than the observed count.
A second acquisition for one recipient displaces the first; the displaced lease cannot claim current ownership and cannot release the live slot.
A new distinct recipient is refused when the registry is full, while a same-recipient handoff stays bounded and is not refused at capacity.
Identical registrations applied in different orders compose an identical route set.
Duplicate, conflicting and over-capacity registrations are refused before the router is sealed, ahead of the axum call that panics.
Refusals name the bound and never the rejected credential, the rejected recipient text, or the observed length.
